data.gender_notes: Venus is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: In Roman mythology, Venus was the goddess of love, beauty, and fertility. She was the mother of Aeneas and the lover of Mars. In Christian spirituality, Venus can symbolize the divine feminine and the love of God. The name Venus carries the meaning “Goddess of love and beauty” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Venus usually hope their child will grow to embody goddess of love and beauty and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Venus total 9, giving a life-path number of 9. Number 9 is linked with Mars and with the qualities of compassion, idealism and generosity.

data.cultural_impact: In Roman mythology, Venus was the most important goddess and the ancestral mater of the Romans. She was the goddess of love, beauty, and fertility, who had the power to make gods and men fall in love. Her festival, the Venalia, was a time for exchanging gifts and settling debts. Venus' temples were popular, and her iconography was widespread, with many Roman villas adorned with images of Venus in various forms. Her love was considered pleasurable and sweet, a true earthly joy.
data.spiritual_significance: In Christian spirituality, Venus can symbolize the divine feminine, the loving, tender side of God, representing compassion, nurture, and God's desire for intimate connection with the human soul. Venus’ imagery and experiential qualities provide a contrast to the traditional Christian emphasis on the masculine divine and can serve to enhance our understanding of God's complex nature. This can lead to a deeper appreciation for the nuanced ways God loves us and responds to us as individuals.
